correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(d\ge3\) and real \(q>q_d\), the proof combines the published exact optimal coefficient, a standard uniform Hankel expansion, zero-mean periodic cancellation yielding a shared \(A_d/(q-q_d)\) divergence and C1 finite Bessel difference, and Xu Theorem 3.9 strict positive zero-cell contributions at q=q_d. Reconstructed exponents: \(2/q_d=(d-1)/d\); difference of 2/q powers therefore has exponent \(1/d\), and the relative slope is \((d-1)L_d/(d A_d)\). All dimensional normalizations follow the Fourier--Bessel identity. A standalone numerical program passed checks in dimensions three and four, not used to infer the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Determines a naturally missing, sharp asymptotic regime of the optimal global stability modulus in the entire fixed-dimensional mixed spherical restriction family. The universal \(1/d\) fractional collapse, exact strictly positive Bessel finite-part coefficient, and simultaneously linear relative gap reveal distinct near-critical behavior despite operator-norm blowup. This is not just a weaker finite-q inequality or arbitrary numerical slice; it establishes a motivated singular limiting law.
